'''''How Data Happened: A History from the Age of Reason to the Age of Algorithms''''' is a 2023 non-fiction book written by [[Columbia University]] professors [[Chris Wiggins (data scientist)|Chris Wiggins]] and [[Matthew L. Jones]]. The book explores the history of data and statistics from the end of the 18th century to the present day.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date= |title=How Data Happened: A History from the Age of Reason to the Age of Algorithms by Chris Wiggins, Matthew L Jones |url=https://www.publishersweekly.com/9781324006732 |access-date=2023-04-27 |website=www.publishersweekly.com}}</ref>

== Content ==
The book starts at the end of the 18th century, when European states began tabulating physical resources, and ends at the present day, when algorithms manipulate our personal information as a commodity. It looks at the rise of data and [[statistics]], and how early statistical methods were used to justify [[eugenics]], quantify supposed racial differences, and develop military and industrial applications. The authors also discuss the impact of the internet and e-commerce on data collection, the rise of [[data science]], and the consequences of government-run [[surveillance]] systems collecting vast amounts of personal data for customized, [[targeted advertising]]. They emphasize the importance of [[privacy]] and [[democracy]] and propose remedies to the problems caused by mass data collection, including stronger regulation of the tech industry and [[collective action]] by its employees. The book is a historical analysis that provides context for understanding the debates surrounding data and its control.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite book |url=https://www.kirkusreviews.com/book-reviews/chris-wiggins/how-data-happened/ |title=HOW DATA HAPPENED {{!}} Kirkus Reviews |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Lepore |first=Jill |date=2023-03-27 |title=The Data Delusion |url=https://www.newyorker.com/magazine/2023/04/03/the-data-delusion |access-date=2023-04-27 |magazine=The New Yorker |language=en-US}}</ref>

The book has 336 pages and was published in 2023 by [[W. W. Norton & Company]].<ref name=":0" />
